title: unified rollouts: metric-driven traffic-shift and automated rollback
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Rolling model versions safely in production requires flexible traffic-shifting, observability-driven gating, and automated rollback when key quality or reliability signals degrade. This PR implements a metric-driven traffic shift controller and a configurable rollback policy that unifies canary, A/B, and shadow workflows under the existing rollouts API.

What this adds: 1) RolloutPolicy resource enhancements to declare metric gates (latency, error-rate, quality-regression) and per-step thresholds; 2) TrafficShiftController: orchestrates percent-based traffic shifts, evaluates Prometheus-adapter metrics at each step, and triggers automated rollback/step-back actions when thresholds are breached; 3) Shadow traffic monitoring: record-only evaluation path so models under shadow don't affect production traffic but are evaluated against the same gates; 4) Integration with the Console's rollout dashboard (backend telemetry + events) for visibility and manual overrides; 5) Safety heuristics: minimum observation window, rate-limited rollback to avoid flapping, and a dry-run mode for validation.

Design notes: The controller evaluates metrics via a generic metrics-adapter interface (Prometheus by default). RolloutPolicy items are evaluated atomically at each step; if any gate fails, the controller can either step-back to the previous percentage or fully rollback depending on policy config. Policies support action: {step-back, full-rollback, pause}. To avoid noisy signals we include smoothing (EMA) and require a minimum sample count.

Testing and rollout plan: unit and integration tests cover controller logic, metric-adapter mocks, and policy evaluation. E2E canary runs were executed in perf-canary with a synthetic workload and a simulated regression to validate automatic rollback timing. The change will be feature-flagged behind rollout_v2 and enabled on a small set of customers for 48h before global enablement.

Backward compatibility: Existing RolloutPolicy manifests without metric gates continue to behave as before (percent-only shifts). New fields are optional and default to conservative behavior (no auto-rollback unless gates are present).

Notes: This PR focuses on orchestration and policy evaluation; model-side optimizations (KV cache behavior during step-up) will be a follow-up (ENG-5240).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) make the default observation window configurable via env var; (2) add telemetry event when controller suppresses a rollback due to min-samples not met.
Asha Patel (author): Addressed both: observation window is now ROLLOUT_OBSERVATION_WINDOW and added suppressed_rollback event. PTAL.
Ravi Gupta: Controller logic looks good. Suggest tightening the EMA smoothing half-life for latency metrics to 10s to reduce lag during fast regressions.
Asha Patel: Reduced EMA half-life to 10s and added comment explaining rationale. Also added unit tests for rapid spike behavior.
Sophie Martinez: Left one nit on naming (stepBack vs rollbackStep). Also asked for an integration test that verifies the console UI picks up events.
Asha Patel: Renamed to step_back for readability and added console integration smoke test. Ready for final review.
Liam Chen: Approved after CI green.
Sophie Martinez: Approved with one non-blocking suggestion to add a short how-to in the docs for creating metric gates.

release_notes:
- Add metric-driven gates to RolloutPolicy for automated rollback
- TrafficShiftController to orchestrate step-based percent shifts with auto-step-back/full rollback actions
- Shadow traffic evaluation path for non-impacting model comparisons
- Console telemetry for rollout events and manual overrides
- Feature-flagged behind rollout_v2; opt-in for canary customers initially
testing: Unit tests covering policy evaluation, transformer of metrics to gate decisions
Integration tests with mocked Prometheus adapter exercising step-back and full-rollback paths
E2E perf-canary: injected regression (increased latency and 5xx) verified that auto-rollback occurred at step 30% within configured observation window
Manual smoke: Console shows rollout event timeline and allows manual pause/abort
